title: Requests, Instructions, and Advice
summary: Making requests, giving simple instructions, and asking for or giving advice.
whyItMatters: Health and household problems often require another person to act. Effective language distinguishes a polite request, a direct instruction, and a suggestion, then checks whether the action is understood and possible.

mentalModel.title: Match force to situation
mentalModel.content: Use a polite modal question for a request, an imperative for a clear instruction, and 'du solltest' or a fixed suggestion for advice.

mentalModel.title: Name action and object
mentalModel.content: Make the desired result visible: 'Bitte bring den Müll raus' is clearer than 'Mach das bitte'.

mentalModel.title: Check the response
mentalModel.content: A complete exchange includes acceptance, clarification, refusal, or confirmation.

ruleBlocks.title: Use modal questions for polite requests
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Kannst du ...?' informally and 'Können Sie ...?' formally, usually with 'bitte'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use a clear imperative for instructions
ruleBlocks.content: Use short action-first forms such as 'Nimm die Tablette' or 'Machen Sie bitte das Fenster zu'.

ruleBlocks.title: Frame advice as a helpful option
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Du solltest ...', 'Am besten ...', or 'Ich würde ...' as learnable advice chunks.

ruleBlocks.title: Respond and clarify
ruleBlocks.content: Accept with 'Ja, mache ich', decline with a brief reason, or ask 'Wann genau?' and 'Wie oft?'.

tables.title: Conversation Toolkit
rows: Kannst du bitte das Fenster zumachen?
Du solltest heute zu Hause bleiben.
Wie oft soll ich das machen?

tables.title: Problem and Response
rows: Ruh dich aus und trink Wasser.

patterns: Kannst du / Können Sie bitte + infinitive?
sentenceStructure: A modal request places the action infinitive at the end.
An imperative normally begins with the action verb.
Use a pronoun only when its reference is clear.
Add frequency or timing to health instructions when needed.

concepts: give short instructions and basic advice
accept, refuse, or clarify an action

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies the symptoms, chores, and home situations that require action.
Pronouns make repeated instructions natural when an object or person is already known.

examples.de: A: Kannst du bitte das Bad putzen? B: Ja, mache ich nach dem Essen.
examples.en: A: Can you please clean the bathroom? B: Yes, I will do it after eating.

examples.de: Können Sie mich bitte morgen zurückrufen?
examples.en: Can you please call me back tomorrow?

examples.de: Nehmen Sie die Tablette morgens und abends.
examples.en: Take the tablet in the morning and evening.

examples.de: Du solltest dich ausruhen und viel trinken.
examples.en: You should rest and drink plenty.

examples.de: Der Müll ist voll. Bring ihn bitte raus.
examples.en: The rubbish bin is full. Please take it out.

commonMistakes.wrong: Kannst du machst das Fenster zu?
commonMistakes.reason: After the modal, use a final infinitive.
Use the full object until the pronoun reference is clear.

commonMistakes.wrong: Nimm die Tablette! to an unfamiliar patient
commonMistakes.reason: Use the formal imperative with an unfamiliar adult.

specialCases: 'Soll ich ...?' asks whether the speaker should perform an action.
'Du solltest ...' is advice rather than a command.
In urgent health situations, direct instructions can be appropriate.
tips: Practice each situation as request, instruction, and advice.
Replace nouns with pronouns only on the second mention.
